memory_candidates.content: In agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/orchestrate-batch-admit.sh (and any script that splices jq source into a bash single-quoted string via a pattern like "$JQ_DEFS"'...'), a possessive apostrophe inside a jq-embedded `#` comment (e.g. "the task's own", "this cycle's candidates") silently terminates the enclosing bash single-quote early, producing either a confusing bash syntax error far from the real line, or a jq compile error. This recurred independently 4+ times across one multi-phase task. Fix: reword to avoid the apostrophe (e.g. "of the task" instead of "the task's"); never use an escaped apostrophe inside the single-quoted region. Grep the region between the opening `"$VAR"'` and the matching closing `'` for a bare `'` before considering any jq-program edit done.

When a plan's per-phase Task bullets say 'assert the current behavior' for a fixture that is explicitly labelled a 'red baseline', but that SAME plan's later-phase Verification sections require the fixture to 'remain red until Phase N' (a fail-now/pass-later progression), the Task bullet's literal wording is describing the target TDD red/green outcome loosely, not a literal instruction to assert today's defective behavior. Prefer the repeated, mechanically-checkable Verification-section signal over a single ambiguous Task-bullet phrase, write the fixture against the TARGET post-fix shape from the start, and record the resolution as a deviation rather than silently picking one reading.

When an admission/scheduling predicate is changed to treat an ABSENT or EMPTY declared value (e.g. file_scope: [] or a missing key) as decision-relevant for the first time, every pre-existing test fixture in the same codebase that co-dispatches 2+ candidates sharing that absent/empty value for an UNRELATED reason (lock refusal, flag-forwarding, territory rendering, etc.) can silently break, because the value that used to be admission-neutral padding is now itself a signal. Before landing such a rule, grep the full test corpus for multi-candidate fixtures sharing the newly-meaningful absent/empty value and give each a distinct, disjoint concrete placeholder value (not empty) unless the fixture is deliberately testing the absence/emptiness itself, in which case split it into its own single-signal batch.
